chunks: 4857 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, "May I be sacrificed for you, how is it that when a man accuses his wife, his testimony is four testimonies by Allah, but when someone else accuses her—whether a father, brother, son, or a stranger—he is flogged with the hadd punishment unless he establishes proof for what he said?"

He said, "Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام was asked about that, and he said: 'When a husband accuses his wife and says: “I saw that with my own eye,” then his testimony is four testimonies by Allah. But if he says that he did not see it, he is told: “Establish proof for what you said,” otherwise he is in the same position as anyone else.'"

And that is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made for the husband an access which He has not made for anyone else, whether a father or a son; and he enters upon her by night and day. So it is permissible for him to say, 'I saw.' But if someone else says, 'I saw,' it is said to him, 'What gave you access to the place in which you saw this, alone by yourself? You are under suspicion, and it is unavoidable that the hadd which Allah has made obligatory upon you be carried out against you.'

key_terms.الزَّوْجَ: the husband, who has a distinct legal standing in this case
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةَ: legal proof or evidentiary proof required to establish a claim
key_terms.شَهَادَاتٍ بِاللَّهِ: solemn sworn testimonies by Allah in the li'an procedure
key_terms.قَذَفَ: accused of adultery or illicit sexual misconduct
key_terms.مَدْخَلًا: a special access or lawful entry unique to the husband

ai.seo_question: Why does a husband have a different ruling from other people when accusing his wife of adultery in li'an?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal distinction in li'an between a husband and other accusers when alleging adultery against a wife. The husband is given a specific legal avenue because of his unique private access to his wife, whereas others must produce formal evidence or face the hadd punishment for false accusation.
